after.worked_solution:
For a type II region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $yz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

We consider the region $R$ as a type II region enclosed between the back surface $x={u}_{1}(y,z)=1$ and the front surface $x={u}_{2}(y,z)=3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070533/assets/339d4658909da42d55a836af93c7fda425bbe8d0ce17f246b73a4ca28cb9f380.png)

So, the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,1\le x\le 3}.
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I *plane* region in the $yz$-plane with the upper curve

$$
{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9\,⟺\,z=\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070533/assets/879425adc3b1e78a7ea6a59740c9d8634ac13f62dea8eedc764bb5f1b07c92c2.png)

Hence, $D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2y\,\text{d}V & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{1}^{3}2y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}[{\int }_{1}^{3}2y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}2y[x]_{x=1}^{x=3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}4y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
For a type II region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $yz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

We consider the region $R$ as a type II region enclosed between the back surface $x={u}_{1}(y,z)=1$ and the front surface $x={u}_{2}(y,z)=3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070533/assets/339d4658909da42d55a836af93c7fda425bbe8d0ce17f246b73a4ca28cb9f380.png)

So, the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,1\le x\le 3}.
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I *plane* region in the $yz$-plane with the upper curve

$$
{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9\,⟺\,z=\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070533/assets/879425adc3b1e78a7ea6a59740c9d8634ac13f62dea8eedc764bb5f1b07c92c2.png)

Hence, $D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2y\,\text{d}V & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{1}^{3}2y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}[{\int }_{1}^{3}2y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}2y[x]_{x=1}^{x=3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{9-{y}^{2}}}4y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{z}^{2}}^{4}xyz\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}yz{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x={z}^{2}}^{x=4}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}yz(\frac{16}{2}-\frac{{z}^{4}}{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}8yz-\frac{1}{2}y{z}^{5}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}8yz-\frac{1}{2}y{z}^{5}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}8yz-\frac{1}{2}y{z}^{5}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}4y[{z}^{2}]_{z=0}^{z=2}-\frac{y}{12}[{z}^{6}]_{z=0}^{z=2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}4y(4-0)-\frac{y}{12}(64-0)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}16y-\frac{16}{3}y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}\frac{32}{3}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{16}{3}{[{y}^{2}]}_{y=-1}^{y=2} \\  & =\frac{16}{3}(4-1) \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}18x\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{yz}18x\,dx\,dz\,dy.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{yz}18x\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{yz}18x\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}[9{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=yz}dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}9(yz)^{2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}9{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}9{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}9{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[3{y}^{2}{z}^{3}]_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{y}^{2}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}3{y}^{2}\,dy & =[{y}^{3}]_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070533/assets/ead71a275dfa4d4a0e07a02400e30f85440b3af8ca5a7f8d0cf0ebed60da8a6a.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 4-2y+3z},
$$

where

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 3}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070533/assets/6e48e66eb003be316573e5b44948fcbce43b07e78fea97a7865ecf5eb4b4404a.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 3,\,\,0\le x\le 4-2y+3z}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{yz}{2}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4-2y+3z}\frac{yz}{2}\,dx\,dz\,dy.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4-2y+3z}\frac{yz}{2}\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{4-2y+3z}\frac{yz}{2}\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{yz}{2}[x]_{x=0}^{x=4-2y+3z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{yz}{2}(4-2y+3z)\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{2}(4yz-2{y}^{2}z+3y{z}^{2})\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{2}(4yz-2{y}^{2}z+3y{z}^{2})\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{2}(4yz-2{y}^{2}z+3y{z}^{2})\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}{[2y{z}^{2}-{y}^{2}{z}^{2}+y{z}^{3}]}_{z=0}^{z=3}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(18y-9{y}^{2}+27y)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(45y-9{y}^{2})\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(45y-9{y}^{2})\,dy & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{45}{2}{y}^{2}-3{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(90-24)-0 \\  & =33.\end{aligned}
$$
